title: David Sacks: AI & crypto czar with investments
summary: Well documented: Sacks served as White House AI and crypto czar under ethics waivers (crypto, March 5, 2025; AI, June/July 2025) while he and Craft Ventures kept 400+ AI-linked investments. The NYT's Nov 30, 2025 investigation counted 708 tech holdings, 449 AI-related and 20 crypto-related, and he coordinated the White House push for the GENIUS Act. His role in the UAE/G42 chip approvals rests on secondary summaries of NYT reporting that he pushed for Emirati chip access; the formal licences came from Commerce/BIS, and no stake in a UAE counterparty is documented. Sacks and the White House deny any conflict, no violation has been found, and the NYT did not allege illegality.

sub_claims.statement: Sacks was the White House AI and crypto czar, serving as a special government employee
sub_claims.finding: He served as an SGE (capped at 130 days a year) while remaining a Craft Ventures partner. He stepped down as czar around March 26-27, 2026 and became PCAST co-chair.

sub_claims.statement: He kept AI and crypto interests through Craft Ventures under ethics waivers
sub_claims.finding: White House Counsel David Warrington's March 5, 2025 crypto waiver acknowledged Craft's remaining crypto stakes (about 3.7% of its assets). A second, AI waiver followed in June or July 2025. More than $200M in crypto holdings was divested ($85M+ of it Sacks's own), but 400+ AI-linked investments remain. The filings give neither the timing of sales nor the value of what remains.

sub_claims.statement: A late-2025 NYT investigation detailed hundreds of AI-related holdings
sub_claims.finding: The NYT story ran Nov 30, 2025 ('Silicon Valley's Man in the White House Is Benefiting Himself and His Friends'). It counted 708 tech investments, 449 AI-related and 20 crypto-related. That is the NYT's own classification; Sacks's filings label 438 holdings as software or hardware.

sub_claims.statement: Sacks helped drive the UAE/G42 chip approvals
sub_claims.finding: Summaries of the NYT's Sept 15, 2025 piece say Sacks was central in pushing for broad chip access for the Emirates, and he took part in negotiating the May 2025 framework. The formal licences came from Commerce/BIS: first Nvidia licences for the UAE in Oct 2025, then up to 35,000 GB300-class chips for G42 in Nov 2025. No source names Sacks as approver or shows him holding a stake in G42 or MGX.

sub_claims.statement: Sacks drove the GENIUS Act while Craft held crypto infrastructure stakes
sub_claims.finding: He coordinated the White House position on the bill and promoted it publicly; Trump signed it on July 18, 2025. The NYT cites Craft's 7.8% stake in BitGo at BitGo's IPO filing, and BitGo custodies USD1 reserves (see C11). No source shows Sacks acting on that overlap.

sub_claims.statement: Sacks and the White House deny any conflict
sub_claims.finding: Sacks called the story a 'nothing burger', said OGE approved his waivers and said he divested hundreds of millions. The White House said OGE required only certain AI divestments. His lawyers at Clare Locke sent the NYT a pre-publication letter, and the NYT stood by its story. Reports of a filed defamation lawsuit are unverified.

corrections: There were two waivers: crypto (March 5, 2025) and AI (June or July 2025; outlets differ).
The NYT investigation is dated Nov 30, 2025 and counted 449 AI-related holdings out of 708 tech investments.
Sacks left the czar post in March 2026 and now co-chairs PCAST.
Formal UAE/G42 chip licences were issued by Commerce/BIS; Sacks's documented role was in policy and negotiation.
denials_and_context: Sacks: the NYT story is a 'nothing burger'; OGE approved his waivers; he divested at substantial cost to his net worth.
White House: Sacks acted appropriately; OGE required divestment only of certain AI holdings.
The NYT did not allege illegality, and no ethics agency has found a violation.
Critics, including Warren, Slotkin, Stansbury and ethics scholar Kathleen Clark, call the waivers inadequate and question his 130-day SGE count.

The New York Times articles and the Senate PDFs could not be fetched directly (blocked hosts); findings rest on multi-outlet search coverage. The search budget ran out before checking BitGo IPO details and post-March-2026 developments.
